name: Die Cut Clear Stickers
seoTitle: Die Cut Clear Stickers: Transparent Vinyl Cut to Shape
seoDescription: Die cut clear stickers on transparent vinyl, cut tight to the artwork with an optional white ink layer, for bottles, glass, packaging and laptops. Free proof.
tagline: Transparent vinyl trimmed to the artwork edge, with white ink where your colors need to stay solid.
quickAnswer: Die cut clear stickers are printed on transparent vinyl and cut to the outline of the artwork, so the surface shows through everywhere the ink does not cover. A white ink layer under the print keeps colors solid on glass, dark bottles and packaging. They suit cosmetics, drinks, candles and laptops. Sizes run from 0.5 inches to 24 by 36 inches, from $0.30 each, 100 piece minimum, produced in 5 to 7 business days after proof approval.
highlights: Material: clear 3 mil vinyl, optional white ink

sections.h2: Why cut a clear sticker to shape when it already disappears
sections.html:
Clear vinyl is not invisible. Hold a square clear sticker on a glass bottle up to a window and you will see the edge of the film as a faint line, and after a month on a shelf that edge has collected dust and fingerprints. Cutting the sticker to the outline of the artwork shrinks that edge to a thin margin that follows the design, so what the customer sees is the print and the bottle, not a plastic square. This page is for that build: clear vinyl, die cut, with a white ink layer added under the colors wherever you need them solid.

Our custom clear stickers page is the sibling. It covers clear vinyl in squares, circles and rounded rectangles, plus clear sheets and rolls for labeling lines, where the straight edge is acceptable or even useful for alignment. Choose that when you label hundreds of identical jars by hand and want the edge as a guide; the custom clear sticker page explains the roll and sheet options. Choose die cut when the sticker is the brand mark itself and any visible edge looks wrong.

sections.h2: White ink: the decision that makes or breaks a clear sticker
sections.html:
Ink on clear vinyl is translucent. A yellow printed straight onto clear film and stuck on a brown bottle reads as muddy olive, and white in the artwork simply vanishes because there is no white ink in a standard CMYK print. The fix is a white ink layer printed first, under the colors, exactly where you want them solid. We build that layer for you and show it on the proof. The usual choices are:

  • White under everything: colors look exactly as they do on a white sticker, with a clear margin around the shape
  • White under the logo only: a tagline or outline stays see-through while the mark stays solid
  • No white at all: the design becomes a tint over the surface, which works for a watermark look on clear glass
  • White as a printed color: white text or lines on a dark bottle, with nothing else behind them
  • Partial white at 50 percent: a frosted look that lets some surface color through

Tell us the surface color when you order, because the right white layer for a clear gin bottle is wrong for a black candle jar. Finishes such as spot UV and matte laminate on clear film sit under our stickers by feature listing.

sections.h2: Getting the proof right on a clear sticker
sections.html:
1. Send the artwork as a vector file or a 300 dpi PNG with a transparent background, so we can see which areas are meant to be clear.
  2. Tell us the surface: the bottle color, the glass, the laptop lid. A photo of the product helps.
  3. We build the white ink layer, draw the cut line with a margin of about 0.0625 inches, and place the design on a simulated version of your surface in the free digital proof.
  4. Check the proof for areas that should be clear but are white, and vice versa. This is the step that catches almost every clear sticker problem.
  5. Approve, and production runs 5 to 7 business days. Delivery by FedEx is free within the United States, 8 to 10 business days in total.

sections.h2: Permanent or removable adhesive on clear vinyl
sections.html:
Clear vinyl takes either adhesive. Permanent is the default for product labels, drinkware and anything sold, because it bonds fully in 24 hours and then resists condensation and hand washing. Removable adhesive is for glass that gets re-dressed: a shop window with seasonal graphics, a display case, a rental laptop. It peels clean for a year or so and can be repositioned once or twice during application.

Removable is not the same as reusable. A clear sticker peeled after months on a window has picked up dust on its adhesive and will not stick well a second time. For graphics that go up and come down repeatedly, our custom reusable sticker page covers the static cling and low-tack builds made for that.

sections.h2: Keeping clear vinyl looking clean after application
sections.html:
Clear film shows what white film hides. Apply to a surface cleaned with isopropyl alcohol and fully dry; any dust under the sticker shows as a dot, and any moisture shows as a silver bubble. Press from the center outward with a card, and prick a trapped bubble with a pin rather than peeling the sticker back, which stretches it. Fingerprints on the face wipe off the laminate with a damp cloth.

Sunlight is the long-term enemy. Unlaminated clear vinyl can take on a faint yellow after two or three years outdoors; the laminated version we ship holds clear longer and protects the white ink layer, which scratches more easily than the colors above it. Indoors on a bottle or a laptop, the sticker outlasts the product. The same care rules apply to the white and specialty films across our full custom sticker range, but clear is the one where skipping the alcohol wipe shows.

faqs.q: Do die cut clear stickers have a visible edge?
faqs.a: A faint one, about 0.0625 inches of clear film around the artwork, which is far less noticeable than the square edge of a standard clear sticker. On glass it reads as a thin highlight in direct light and disappears at normal viewing distance. Keeping the surface clean before application keeps the edge from collecting dust.

faqs.q: Why do my colors look faded on a die cut clear sticker?
faqs.a: Because standard inks are translucent and there is no white film behind them. On a dark or colored surface the surface shows through the ink. The fix is a white ink layer printed under the colors, which we add for you and show on the proof. With it, colors look the same as they would on white vinyl.

faqs.q: Can die cut clear stickers go on a dark bottle?
faqs.a: Yes, with a white ink underprint. On amber, green or black glass the white layer gives the colors something to sit on, so a yellow stays yellow instead of turning olive. Ask for white under the whole design on dark bottles; a partial white layer is better reserved for clear glass where you want some see-through areas.

faqs.q: Are die cut clear stickers waterproof on drinkware?
faqs.a: Yes. Clear vinyl is a plastic film and the adhesive is water resistant, so a bottle or tumbler can be hand washed and go through condensation without the sticker lifting. Let it cure for 24 hours after application. For dishwasher use, order the laminated version so the white ink layer is protected from hot cycles.

faqs.q: Can die cut clear stickers be removed and reused?
faqs.a: Removed, yes; reused, not reliably. Removable adhesive peels clean from glass for about a year, but the adhesive picks up dust once it has been off the surface and will not re-bond well. For graphics that go up and down repeatedly, a static cling or low-tack reusable sticker is the right product.

faqs.q: What is the thinnest line a clear die cut sticker can print?
faqs.a: Keep lines at 0.5 point or thicker in color, and 0.75 point or thicker if they are white ink only, because the white layer is printed separately and very fine white lines can look broken. Text should stay at 6 point or above. Thin outlines around a shape are better set as a printed border than as a cut line.

faqs.q: Do die cut clear stickers yellow in sunlight?
faqs.a: Unlaminated clear vinyl can show a faint yellow tint after two or three years of direct sun, mostly on vehicles and outdoor windows. The laminated version holds clear longer. Indoors, on bottles, laptops and packaging, there is no measurable change over the life of the product.

faqs.q: Can I print white text on die cut transparent stickers?
faqs.a: Yes. White is printed as its own ink layer on clear vinyl, so white lettering and line art print cleanly with nothing behind them, which looks striking on a dark bottle or a black laptop. Keep white text at 7 point or larger, since it is printed in a single pass and very small white type can soften.

faqs.q: Will die cut clear stickers show bubbles on glass?
faqs.a: Only if air or dust gets trapped during application, and clear film shows both as silver spots. Clean the glass with isopropyl alcohol, let it dry, and press the sticker from the center outward with a card. If a bubble remains, pierce it with a pin and press flat rather than lifting the sticker, which stretches the film.

faqs.q: How many die cut clear stickers do I need to order?
faqs.a: 100 per design is the minimum. Pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker and rises with size, the white ink layer and lamination. If you want to test a bottle label before a larger run, order the 100 and apply a few to real product; the behavior on your glass is the thing a proof cannot fully show.

faqs.q: Can die cut clear stickers be matte instead of glossy?
faqs.a: Yes. A matte laminate over clear vinyl gives a frosted, low-glare finish that photographs well on cosmetics and candles. It softens the surface slightly, so the see-through areas look lightly frosted rather than glass clear. Gloss keeps the surface fully transparent and the colors at their most saturated.

faqs.q: How long do die cut clear stickers take to produce?
faqs.a: Production takes 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free proof, and FedEx delivery is free within the United States, so plan on 8 to 10 business days in total. The white ink layer does not add time. If you are launching a product on a date, mention it on the quote and we will say whether a rush is possible.
